hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Alternative a2 wins: one canonical TypeScript type per Story (Pointer/Locator, Scope, ReviewTargets, CommentEntry+round), with per-review-type validator functions running against the canonical type and a thin per-consumer transformer reshaping it for whichever LLM structured-output schema that consumer actually parses reliably, mirroring the existing CliProvider input/output transformer pattern.

ownedContracts.name: ReviewTargets
ownedContracts.purpose: The submitter-owned, fully-reset-each-round list of content to review this round, per lc3/lc4.

consumedContracts.name: Locator + Pointer
consumedContracts.purpose: The uniform way every Scope and ReviewTargets entry names a piece of content: a Pointer to an existing authored file plus an optional Locator pinning an exact region within it, per k2.

consumedContracts.name: Pointer staleness check
consumedContracts.purpose: One staleness-detection function signature shared by every Pointer consumer (Scope and ReviewTargets alike), per k5 -- no consumer defines its own.

consumedContracts.name: Pointer path validation
consumedContracts.purpose: One repo-root-escape check shared by every Pointer consumer (Scope and ReviewTargets alike), per the Epic's own nonFunctional security note -- no consumer defines its own, mirroring sc2's staleness-check pattern. Closes a cross-Story gap found in a controller-led cross-LLD review on 2026-11-19: s1's error-paths deferred this check to 's2's ScopeValidator' informally, but neither s2 nor s3 ever picked it up.

boundary.internal: ReviewTargets' own reset-on-new-round mechanics (how the entries list is rebuilt rather than merged) stay internal to s3; no other Story's type depends on ReviewTargets.

adjacentBoundaries.internal: The specific set of currently-known LocatorKind string literals (symbol/lineRange/docSection) is s1's own enumeration; because every consumer treats `Locator.kind` as an opaque string rather than exhaustively switching on a closed union, s1 can add a new literal later without forcing s2/s3/s4 to change, satisfying ac2/lc1.

Which named artifact-kind fields Scope carries beyond def/hld/lld/plan/tasks (e.g. a future named kind) and the exact per-review-type ScopeValidator implementations are s2's own; no other Story's type depends on Scope, since nothing in the Epic's Story graph consumes s2.

CommentEntry does not reference Pointer/Locator at all, so s4 needs neither sc1 nor sc2. The round-stamping mechanics (how a new attempt's round number is assigned) and the same-artifact-only scoping of Comments across a chain stay internal to s4; the full ReviewContext container embedding Scope and ReviewTargets alongside round/comments is explicitly deferred (Epic Non-Goals), since no Story in this graph depends on all of s2, s3 and s4 together.

hldContextSlice.rolloutPhase: Phase B — Scope, ReviewTargets and Comments types

nonFunctional.performance: The staleness check (sc2) is a single hash comparison against already-read file content; it adds no I/O beyond the read the controller already performs to populate a Pointer's contentHash.
nonFunctional.security: Pointer.path is repo-relative and must resolve within the registered repo root; validators (k3) reject a Pointer whose path escapes that root, consistent with the repo-registry strict-contract rule elsewhere in this codebase.

summary.prose: This Story defines ReviewTargets, the submitter-owned list naming exactly the content to review this round. It is deliberately minimal: a single readonly list of Pointer entries, rebuilt fresh every round with no builder or merge function of any kind, so there is no API surface that could ever merge or carry forward a prior round's targets.

dataModelChanges.details: interface ReviewTargets { readonly entries: readonly Pointer[] }, exactly as sc4's interfaceSketch. entries is rebuilt fresh every round from that round's real target set; this Story provides no builder, factory or merge function -- a caller constructs a fresh object literal each round. Entries carry no origin metadata beyond what Pointer itself already carries (per lc4), and the reviewer is never restricted to only these entries (per ac2). Lands in src/workflow/artifact-core/types.ts alongside sc1/sc2/sc3's types.

interactionWithShared.howDetails: This Story is sc4's owner; ReviewTargets is implemented exactly as sc4's interfaceSketch, with zero additional API surface.
ReviewTargets.entries is typed as readonly Pointer[] exactly as sc1 publishes Pointer; this Story does not redesign Locator or Pointer.

This Story does not call PointerStalenessCheck itself; it simply ensures entries stays structurally compatible with sc2's PointerStalenessCheck signature for whichever caller later runs that check per-entry.

ReviewTargets carries no validator of its own (a1's deliberate choice); the caller that assembles a ReviewTargets is responsible for running sc6's PointerPathValidator (owned by s1) against each entry before sending it for review, the same caller-invoked pattern this Story already documents for sc2's PointerStalenessCheck. Closes a gap a cross-LLD review found: previously nothing named this responsibility for ReviewTargets' entries at all.

errorCases.scenario: A caller concatenates or spreads the previous round's ReviewTargets.entries into the new round's array before constructing the new ReviewTargets, instead of building purely from the current round's real target set.
errorCases.detection: None exists in this Story's own surface: ReviewTargets' type accepts any readonly Pointer[] value, and there is no field, flag or function that could distinguish a freshly-sourced array from one that includes carried-over entries.
errorCases.response: Not caught by this Story's contract at all -- lc3/ac1 are enforced entirely by controller discipline outside ReviewTargets' own boundary, since the smallest-shape alternative (a1) deliberately provides no builder or merge-detection mechanism.
errorCases.userImpact: A caller that violates lc3 would silently produce a ReviewTargets that looks structurally identical to a correctly-built one; no error surfaces at the type level.

errorCases.scenario: A Pointer inside entries names a path that no longer exists (e.g. deleted since this round's target set was computed).
errorCases.detection: ReviewTargets performs no I/O and no existence check -- it is a plain data holder with no behavior of its own.
errorCases.response: Out of this Story's scope: sourcing entries correctly from 'the current real set of targets' is the caller's responsibility; any resulting file-read failure surfaces wherever a consumer later reads that Pointer's path, not inside ReviewTargets.
errorCases.userImpact: None directly from this Story's types.

errorCases.scenario: A Pointer inside entries carries a path that would resolve outside the registered repo root (e.g. containing '..' segments).
errorCases.detection: ReviewTargets itself performs no check (it is a plain data holder); detection is the caller's responsibility, by running sc6's PointerPathValidator against each entry before sending the ReviewTargets for review -- the same caller-invoked pattern this Story already uses for sc2's PointerStalenessCheck.
errorCases.response: Not caught by ReviewTargets' own type, by design (mirrors sc2's caller-invoked pattern). Closes a gap a cross-LLD review found: previously no Story's LLD named this responsibility for ReviewTargets' entries at all; the caller must now call sc6's PointerPathValidator per entry, exactly as it is expected to call sc2's PointerStalenessCheck per entry.
errorCases.userImpact: A caller that skips running PointerPathValidator on ReviewTargets' entries could still send an escaping Pointer for review; the Story's own contract makes this an explicit caller responsibility rather than silently unaddressed.

edgeCases.input: entries is an empty array (e.g. a round where no files actually changed, such as a metadata-only edit).
edgeCases.expected: Valid -- ReviewTargets with zero entries is structurally fine; ac2 still lets the reviewer investigate any file or region freely regardless of how many entries the floor set names.

edgeCases.input: entries contains the same Pointer (same path and section) listed twice.
edgeCases.expected: Accepted without special-casing -- sc4's interfaceSketch does not forbid duplicate entries, and this Story introduces no deduplication logic.

edgeCases.input: entries mixes whole-file Pointers (no section) with region-pinned Pointers (section populated).
edgeCases.expected: Both accepted -- Pointer's own optional section field governs this per sc1, and ReviewTargets places no constraint on which of its entries carry a section.

alternativesConsidered.name: Bare ReviewTargets interface exactly as sketched, no accompanying API
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: ReviewTargets{entries: readonly Pointer[]} exactly as sc4's interfaceSketch, with no builder, factory or merge function of any kind -- the 'reset each round, never merged' rule (lc3) is a controller-usage discipline this Story documents but does not enforce through extra API surface.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Define interface ReviewTargets { readonly entries: readonly Pointer[] } and nothing else. A caller builds a new ReviewTargets each round by constructing a fresh object literal from that round's real target set; there is no exported function to call, no state ReviewTargets itself tracks across rounds, and no mechanism this Story provides to merge two ReviewTargets instances together (none exists to misuse).
pros: Matches sc4's interfaceSketch exactly -- the smallest shape that fully satisfies ac1/ac2/lc3/lc4
Adds zero API surface nobody asked for: the HLD never asks for a builder or factory, only the plain interface

There being no merge-capable function anywhere in this Story's surface is itself a stronger guarantee against lc3 violation than a convention comment could be -- the capability to merge simply does not exist to misuse
cons: The 'rebuilt fresh every round, never merged with a prior round's entries' rule is enforced entirely by caller discipline and documentation, not by any type-level or runtime check this Story provides

alternativesConsidered.name: A buildReviewTargets factory function wrapping the entries array
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Add a buildReviewTargets(pointers: readonly Pointer[]) => ReviewTargets factory that every caller is expected to use each round, instead of constructing the object literal directly.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Export a function buildReviewTargets that takes this round's real Pointer list and returns a ReviewTargets wrapping it, with no other behavior -- callers would use this function rather than writing the object literal themselves.
pros: Gives callers one named entry point to use each round, which could read as a clearer signal of 'this is how you build a fresh ReviewTargets'
cons: The function would do nothing beyond `{ entries: pointers }` -- a pure pass-through wrapper adds API surface and an import for zero behavioral guarantee, since nothing stops a caller from still writing the object literal directly instead of calling it
No Story acceptance criterion or HLD contract asks for a builder function; sc4's own interfaceSketch publishes only the bare interface
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Satisfies every ac/sc/k constraint but scores only partial on sc4 for adding a pass-through buildReviewTargets builder that sc4's own interfaceSketch does not publish or require, with no real behavioral guarantee since a caller can still bypass it.

alternativesConsidered.name: A mergeReviewTargets function combining a new round's entries with the previous round's
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Export a mergeReviewTargets(previous: ReviewTargets, next: ReviewTargets) => ReviewTargets that unions or appends entries across rounds instead of discarding the previous round's list.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Provide a function that takes the prior round's ReviewTargets and the new round's raw entries and produces a combined ReviewTargets carrying both.
pros: Could seem convenient if a caller wanted continuity of what was reviewed across rounds
cons: Directly contradicts lc3 ('ReviewTargets is fully reset, not merged or carried forward, on every new review round') and ac1 ('no entries merged or carried forward from the previous round') -- this alternative provides exactly the capability those constraints exist to forbid
Would mislead a future caller into believing merging is the sanctioned way to build ReviewTargets, the opposite of what sc4's purpose statement requires
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Violates ac1 and sc4 directly by providing a mergeReviewTargets capability that lc3 and sc4's own interfaceSketch comment explicitly forbid.

erDefinition.narrative: Shows ReviewTargets' single relationship: a one-to-many, rebuilt-fresh-each-round list of Pointer entries naming the content to review.

ReviewTargets.description: The submitter-owned, fully-reset-each-round list of content to review this round; never merged with a prior round's entries.

entries.description: The current round's real target set, rebuilt fresh every round.

Pointer.description: Owned by sibling Story s1 (sc1) -- references an existing authored file directly. Shown here only as the range target for ReviewTargets.entries; not redesigned by this Story.

path.description: Repo-relative path to an existing authored file.

section.description: An optional Locator pinning the exact region within path this Pointer names.

contentHash.description: sha256 hex digest of path's content when this Pointer was built.

Locator.description: Owned by sibling Story s1 (sc1) -- pins an exact region within an authored file via an open (non-exhaustive) kind discriminant. Shown here only as the range target for Pointer.section; not redesigned by this Story.

kind.description: LocatorKind | string -- read structurally, never via exhaustive switch.

value.description: One opaque string formatted per kind.
